Style code and local writing

On this page

analyzeText ​

Analyze a text string and return heuristic scores and text counts.

Syntax ​

javascript
const result = WriteLikeMe.analyzeText(text);

Parameters ​

ParameterTypeDescription
textstringText to analyze. Non-string values return the empty-input result.

Returns ​

PropertyTypeCurrent behavior
formalitynumber (0-1)Keyword ratio from a small set of formal and casual words
complexitynumber (0-1)Average word length and proportion of words with seven or more characters
sentence_lengthnumber (0-1)Average words per sentence, normalized against 30 words
vocabularynumber (0-1)Unique-token count adjusted by the square root of total token count
tonenumber (0-1)Ratio of words in small positive/negative keyword lists; 0.5 if neither appears
creativitynumber (0-1)Weighted combination of vocabulary variety, imagery keywords, and punctuation variety
punctuationnumber (0-1)Share of commas among commas and periods; 0.5 when neither appears
confidencenumber (0-1)Word count divided by 200, capped at 1; not statistical confidence
wordCountnumberCount of Unicode letter/number tokens
charCountnumberUTF-16 code-unit count after trimming leading and trailing whitespace
commaCountnumberNumber of comma characters
periodCountnumberNumber of period characters
commaSharenumber (0-1)Same comma-to-period balance as punctuation
semicolonCount, colonCount, dashCountnumberCounts of these punctuation marks
questionCount, exclamationCountnumberQuestion and exclamation mark counts
first_person, second_personnumber (0-1)Scaled rates of first- and second-person pronouns
contraction_ratenumber (0-1)Scaled contraction frequency
sentence_variationnumber (0-1)Coefficient of variation for sentence lengths, capped at 1
paragraph_lengthnumber (0-1)Average paragraph word count normalized against 60 words
question_rate, exclamation_ratenumber (0-1)Mark counts per sentence, capped at 1
transition_rate, hedging_ratenumber (0-1)Scaled frequency of words from small English-language lists
frequentWordsstring[]Up to five most frequent content words, excluding a small common-word list

Non-string, empty, and whitespace-only input returns the default category values, zero confidence, zero word/character/punctuation counts, zero voice-cue scores, an empty frequentWords list, and neutral punctuation balance.

The punctuation signal measures comma-versus-period habits, not grammatical correctness. Its SVG band uses comma-shaped marks and period dots to make that balance visually distinct.

Example ​

javascript
const WriteLikeMe = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme');

const result = WriteLikeMe.analyzeText('Hello, world!');
console.log(result.wordCount); // 2
console.log(result.charCount); // 13
console.log(result.complexity); // 0.28
console.log(result.vocabulary); // 0.57
console.log(result.confidence); // 0.01

Tokenization recognizes Unicode letters and numbers. The keyword lists are small, English-focused, and do not understand context, negation, sarcasm, or word meaning outside the listed terms. The sentence and word-length metrics are simple proxies. Results are experimental, may be inaccurate (especially for short text or other languages), and must not be treated as a reliable linguistic or psychological measurement or used for consequential decisions.

Compare a draft with a reference ​

Use compareTextStyle(referenceText, candidateText) to check whether an AI draft resembles the user's analyzed style:

javascript
const comparison = WriteLikeMe.compareTextStyle(userSample, generatedDraft);
console.log(comparison.similarity); // 0-1 heuristic similarity
console.log(comparison.differences.formality); // Absolute difference for a style signal
console.log(comparison.differences.frequentWordsOverlap); // 0-1 word overlap

similarity is the average similarity across the seven SVG categories, numeric voice cues, and frequent-word overlap, rounded to two decimal places. differences contains the absolute difference for each numeric signal and frequentWordsOverlap, the Jaccard overlap of the two frequentWords lists (higher is a closer match). It compares style cues, not meaning, and cannot guarantee that a draft sounds like its author. If either text has no analyzable words, similarity is 0.

The SVG's visible pattern uses the seven categories accepted by generateStyleSVG. Its embedded metadata also stores the additional voice-cue scores and frequent words; these are not separate SVG bands. Use readStyleCode(svg) to retrieve that profile.
